Olga / Sarah —

Looping in security and evidence ops. Below is the packaging checklist we will follow; share any procurement constraints and we'll adapt.

Required packaging checklist (Redwood standard for split-export uploads):

- PDF handling
  - Flatten all PDFs, embed fonts, remove active form fields and JavaScript.
  - Apply redaction rectangles rather than whiteout where required. For each redacted file, include a separate redaction map row (file, pages redacted, rationale).
  - Create an audit footer on redacted pages: "Redacted by Redwood Inference — reason: [X] — date: YYYY-MM-DD" (so auditors can see redaction provenance).

- Evidence index (SIG_evidence_index_v1.csv)
  - Columns: filename, original_question_id, internal_doc_id, sha256_hex, file_size_bytes, redaction_required, pages_redacted, redaction_reason, cust_visibility (public/internal/PHI_adjacent)

- Manifests & Checksums
  - Provide a top-level manifest CSV and a checksums file (SHA256SUMS.txt).
  - Checksums must be computed on the final flattened PDF bytes.

- Portal upload considerations
  - Whistic: prefers one ZIP per request with index CSV and SHA256SUMS.txt. Confirmed max zipped upload ~500MB per upload.
  - OneTrust: supports chunked uploads; metadata fields (document_type, control_ref, question_ref) must be populated. OneTrust sometimes strips special characters; normalize filenames to [A-Za-z0-9_\-\.].

- Naming convention
  - Use: GLH_[questionID]_[short-description]_[v1].pdf (e.g., GLH_Q12_Access-Control_Policy_v1.pdf)

- Quality checks (post-build)
  - Spot-check 10 random PDFs open correctly, checksums match, and redaction footer present.
  - Verify index row count == number of PDF files.

I attached a starter index template and a redaction-map template so ops can begin formatting. We'll also include a small helper script for compute + packaging.

Marissa

Couple of portal-specific notes from the ops side:

- Whistic uploads: they accept a ZIP containing the PDFs + index. They will auto-scan the CSV for matching filenames. Keep ZIP <= 480MB to be safe.
- OneTrust: if procurement chooses OneTrust, we need to populate the control_ref and question_ref columns in the CSV; also their API rate-limits chunked uploads so our automation will backoff.
- Chunking strategy: for >480MB, we recommend chunking into 400MB ZIPs and include a top-level master_manifest.csv that maps which zip contains each file.

I'll attach the small packaging script we use (bash + sha256sum calls) and the internal runbook link. Ops can run: ./portal_batch_script.sh --source evidence_dir --target whistic --email procurement@greenlinehealth.com

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
